chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Bureid ibn Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
We found in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, while he was upon his pulpit:

By the One, there is no god except Him, a believer is never given the good of this world and the Hereafter except by the goodness of his hope/thoughts in Allah, and his hopefulness to Him, and the goodness of his character, and the restraint from backbiting the believers.

By the One, there is no god except Him, Allah does not punish a believer after repentance and seeking forgiveness except by the evil of his hope/thoughts in Allah, and his deficiency in his hopefulness, and the evil of his character, and his backbiting of the believers.

By the One, there is no god except Him, the hope/thought of a believing servant in Allah will not be good unless Allah is according to the hope/thought of His believing servant, because Allah is Generous. In His Hand are the good things. He is bashful that His believing servant should have good thoughts about Him, then He should disappoint his thought and his hope.
So have good thoughts about Allah, and yearn towards Him.

key_terms.حُسْنُ الظَّنِّ: Good hope or good thoughts in Allah
key_terms.سُوءُ الظَّنِّ: Bad hope or bad thoughts in Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a believer to receive the best of this world and the Hereafter according to the Book of Ali?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Ibn Mahbub in Al-Kafi, this hadith establishes 'husn al-zann' (good expectation) as the pivotal spiritual mechanism linking divine generosity to human conduct, specifically highlighting the interplay between internal hope and external ethics like avoiding backbiting. It underscores the Shia theological concept that Allah’s 'Karam' (generosity/bashfulness) ensures He does not disappoint the believer who places sincere trust in Him, thereby making positive expectation a prerequisite for sustained spiritual success.
